title: Retrieve a soup can from the gap beside a cabinet
instruction: Please get the soup can out from between the cabinet side and the wall, and leave it standing in the marked area beside the gap. Keep it upright and avoid scraping either panel.
context: Retrieving a fallen pantry item requires fitting the robot hand itself into a restricted gap and directly grasping the can without tipping it. Unlike pulling an exposed cord (#182), replacing a filter behind a glove box (#1957), or using a reacher-grabber (#2376), this task provides no tool or remote handle.
setup: Station table, top 0.7475 m; x forward, y left. One upright YCB steel tomato soup can with a paper label and sealed contents, scaled widest horizontal dimension 66.000 mm, other horizontal dimension 65.899 mm, height 99.249 mm, mass 414.1 g. It starts centred at x 0.140 m, y -0.080 m, with a 1 mm bottom-to-table spawn gap. Two fixed rectangular panels represent a light wood cabinet side and a grey painted-plaster wall: each 240 mm long along x, 18 mm thick, 114.249 mm high, with their bottoms on the table and their x centres at 0.140 m. Their inner faces are 71.999 mm apart, symmetrically around y -0.080 m; the can is between them. The table forms the gap floor. A pale 100 by 100 mm rectangular landing outline centred at x 0.140 m, y -0.220 m consists of four fixed 2 mm wide, 0.5 mm high plastic marking strips: two 100 mm strips along y and two 96 mm strips along x, meeting without overlap. The centre area is bare table. No other task objects.
scoring: Highest satisfied tier at the end; tiers do not add. Any observed can tilt of 5 degrees or more, can leaving the table, invalid initial layout, displaced fixed structure, or unexplained can displacement over 100 mm in one control step latches zero for the episode; later restoration does not erase it. Otherwise: 0.25 when the entire upright can is out of the finite gap prism; 0.5 when it is also supported on the table (bottom no more than 3 mm above or 2 mm below the tabletop, vertical position spread at most 2 mm over the 10-frame window; before the window fills, vertical speed at most 30 mm/s); 0.75 when its centre is also within 15 mm of the marked centre along each horizontal axis and every pair of positions in the latest 10-frame window differs by at most 2 mm. Before 10 samples, stillness uses speed below 10 mm/s and spin below 0.2 rad/s. Upright means tilt less than 5 degrees, independent of yaw. Full 1.0 requires the 0.75 conditions continuously for 1 s through the framework success hold. In real trials, the gripper is open and at least 30 mm from the can at the end, judged from the trial video. Simulation scoring uses only object states and cannot independently observe release.
fidelity: The actual Arena YCB can mesh is used with the library asset collision decomposition, a mass preserving its estimated filled density after uniform scaling, and automatic library mass properties. The two panels are fixed analytic boxes representing planar cabinet/wall surfaces; their rigidity, friction, and immobility are approximations. Planar marking strips do not support the can. CPU URDF kinematics and collision-hull geometry were verified; GPU PhysX grip, slip, rest pose, camera visibility, and full-score execution remain pending. Release is checked from the video rather than inferred from object velocity. Stock framework grasp materials use static/dynamic friction 1.2/1.0, which is a simplifying high-friction contact model; the can contact offset is 5 mm with zero rest offset. Contact offsets on other colliders and early contacts require GPU verification.
reset_notes: Place the can upright between the panels at the nominal marked position and restore the fixed layout. Episode history clears only when a one-step displacement over 100 mm returns the can to the nominal layout; slowly putting it back cannot clear a violation. Use object_jitter=0 for the scripted demo. No consumed objects.
